responsibility: This module covers GCC’s late RTL backend machinery for register allocation, reload/constraint satisfaction, and instruction scheduling, along with the shared register metadata those passes depend on. Its IRA files build regional allocation IR, compute liveness, costs, conflicts, color allocnos, and rewrite RTL to realize regional assignments, while the LRA and legacy reload families satisfy target operand/address constraints through iterative live-range rebuilding, assignment, spilling, rematerialization, elimination, and final substitution. Surrounding register passes and infrastructure handle core register information and sets, hard-register notes, post-allocation cleanup and improvement such as hard-register copy propagation, renaming, and stack-register conversion for stack-like FP targets. The scheduling side provides dependence analysis plus multiple RTL schedulers—Haifa block/region/EBB scheduling and selective scheduling with pipelining—used to reorder already-generated RTL insns according to data/control dependences, target issue constraints, and speculation policies. Together these files define the backend stage that turns generic RTL into target-constrained, register-assigned, and schedule-optimized RTL ready for final emission.
